blurb.en: Describe people, places and things in 6 to 8 clear sentences.
blurb.vi: Miêu tả người, nơi chốn và đồ vật bằng 6 đến 8 câu rõ ràng.

title.vi: Từ miêu tả nơi chốn và đồ vật
Từ nối và từ về bài viết

kind.def: Nice to other people and happy to help them.
kind.ex: My grandma is very *kind* to everyone.

funny.ex: My uncle tells *funny* stories at dinner.

friendly.def: Happy to talk to people, and smiles a lot.

helpful.def: Often does things that make your work easier.
helpful.ex: My big brother is *helpful* when I have homework.

clever.def: Quick to learn and understand things.
clever.ex: Our coach is *clever* and knows lots of games.

huge.ex: The museum has a *huge* glass door.

quiet.ex: The reading room is *quiet* in the morning.

colourful.def: With lots of bright reds, blues, greens and yellows.

useful.def: Good for doing a job or for helping you.
useful.ex: A torch is *useful* when the lights go off.

because.def: A linking word that gives a reason.
because.ex: I love my aunt *because* she is so kind.

but.def: A linking word that joins two different ideas.
but.ex: The lamp is small, *but* it is very bright.

also.def: A word that adds one more idea.
also.ex: He is funny. He is *also* very clever.

paragraph.def: A group of sentences about one topic.
paragraph.ex: Write all your sentences in one *paragraph*.

scenes.head: Task 1: Esme writes about her uncle
scenes.html: My favourite person is my uncle. He is a cook in a busy restaurant. He is tall, *funny* and very *kind*. Every Sunday he cooks noodles for our family, *and* he *also* teaches me to make spring rolls. He is special to me *because* he always makes me laugh.

steps.en: Esme answers all four questions: who he is, what he is like, what he does and why he is special.
steps.vi: Esme trả lời đủ bốn câu hỏi: chú là ai, chú như thế nào, chú làm gì và vì sao chú đặc biệt.

steps.en: The describing words *funny* and *kind* tell us what he is like.
steps.vi: Các từ miêu tả *funny* và *kind* cho ta biết chú là người như thế nào.

steps.en: The linking words *and*, *also* and *because* join her ideas.
steps.vi: Các từ nối *and*, *also* và *because* nối các ý của bạn ấy lại với nhau.

steps.en: Her last sentence gives a reason: He is special to me *because* ...
steps.vi: Câu cuối nêu lý do: He is special to me *because* ...

scenes.head: Task 2: Hieu writes about a solar lamp
scenes.html: In our garden there is a small solar lamp. It is next to the front door. It is black and silver, with a *tiny* blue light. On top, there is a solar panel. We use it *to catch* sunlight in the day. At night, the lamp turns on by itself. I like it *because* it is *useful* and it doesn't waste energy.

steps.en: First, Hieu names the thing and says where we can find it: a solar lamp next to the front door.
steps.vi: Đầu tiên, Hieu nói đó là gì và ở đâu: một chiếc đèn năng lượng mặt trời cạnh cửa trước.

steps.en: Next, he says what it looks like: black and silver, with a *tiny* blue light.
steps.vi: Tiếp theo, bạn ấy tả hình dáng: màu đen và bạc, có một bóng đèn xanh *tí hon*.

steps.en: The special feature is the solar panel. *We use it to catch* sunlight: to + verb says what it is for.
steps.vi: Đặc điểm đặc biệt là tấm pin mặt trời. *We use it to catch* sunlight: to + động từ cho biết nó dùng để làm gì.

steps.en: He ends with his opinion and a reason: I like it *because* ...
steps.vi: Bạn ấy kết bài bằng ý kiến và lý do: I like it *because* ...

scenes.head: Rory's sentences: before and after checking
scenes.html:
Before: my big sister *are* very kind she *like* cats and she has a *beautifull* cat.

After: *My* big sister *is* very kind. *She likes* cats, and she has a *beautiful* cat.

steps.en: Start every sentence with a *capital letter* and end it with a *full stop*.
steps.vi: Bắt đầu mỗi câu bằng *chữ in hoa* và kết thúc bằng *dấu chấm*.

steps.en: Check the verb: he, she and it need the right form: she *is*, she *likes*.
steps.vi: Kiểm tra động từ: he, she, it cần đúng dạng: she *is*, she *likes*.

steps.en: Check words you know well: *beautiful* has only one l at the end.
steps.vi: Kiểm tra những từ quen thuộc: *beautiful* chỉ có một chữ l ở cuối.

end.en: Great work! You can describe, link and check your sentences.
end.vi: Làm tốt lắm! Bạn đã biết miêu tả, nối câu và kiểm tra câu văn.

challenge.result: You chose the best describing words, linking words and missing bullet points.

v.q: 'My grandpa tells jokes all day. He is very ______.' Choose the best word.
whys: A quiet person does not talk much, but Grandpa tells jokes all day.
'Huge' is for big things like buildings, not for jokes.
v.hint: Read the first sentence. What kind of person tells jokes?
v.worked: Someone who tells jokes makes people laugh, so he is *funny*.

v.q: 'The museum has more than a hundred rooms. It is ______.' Choose the best word.
whys: A building with a hundred rooms can't be tiny.
'Friendly' describes people, not buildings.
v.hint: Think about the size. Is a hundred rooms a lot?
v.worked: More than a hundred rooms is very, very big, so the museum is *huge*.

v.q: 'I like my neighbour ______ she is very friendly.' Choose the best word.
whys: 'But' joins two different ideas. Being friendly is a reason to like her.
'Then' tells us what happens next, not a reason.
v.hint: Is the second part a reason, a different idea or the next thing?
v.worked: 'She is very friendly' is the reason, so we use *because*.

v.q: 'The lamp is very small, ______ it is very bright.' Choose the best word.
whys: Being small is not the reason it is bright.
'So' shows a result, but small things are not bright because they are small.
v.hint: Are the two ideas the same kind of idea, or different?
v.worked: Small and bright are surprising together, so we use *but*.

v.q: 'We use the big pot ______ soup.' Choose the best words.
whys: We don't say 'use the big pot cooking soup'. Use 'to' + verb to say what it is for.
'Cooks' is for he, she or it, not after 'the big pot'.
v.hint: To say what something is for, use: to + verb.
v.worked: 'We use the big pot *to cook* soup' tells us what the pot is for.

v.q: 'The robot has a long arm ______ up rocks.' Choose the best words.
whys: 'Picked' is the past. We need to say what the arm is for.
'Has a long arm picks' is not a correct sentence.
v.hint: What is the arm for? Use: to + verb.
v.worked: 'A long arm *to pick* up rocks' tells us what the arm is for.

v.q: The task asks: who the person is, what he or she is like, what he or she does, why the person is special. Layla wrote: 'My aunt is a nurse. She is calm and kind. She works at a big hospital.' What is missing?
opts: who her aunt is and her job
whys: 'She is calm and kind' tells us what her aunt is like.
'My aunt is a nurse' tells us who she is and her job.
v.hint: Tick each bullet point. Which one has no tick?
v.worked: There is no reason with 'because', so the last bullet point is missing.

v.q: The task asks: what it is and where, what it looks like, one special feature and its use, why you like it. Ivan wrote: 'There is a big clock in our town square. It is white and very tall. I like it because it is beautiful.' What is missing?
opts: a special feature and its use
what the clock in the square looks like
whys: 'White and very tall' tells us what it looks like.
'I like it because it is beautiful' is his reason.
v.hint: Look for 'to + verb'. Does Ivan say what something is for?
v.worked: Ivan does not say one special feature or what it is for, for example 'It has bells to tell the time'.

blurb.en: Practise describing words, linking words and checking your sentences.
blurb.vi: Luyện từ miêu tả, từ nối và cách kiểm tra câu văn.

title.vi: Từ miêu tả và từ nối

v.q: 'My aunt always helps her neighbours. She is very ______.' Choose the best word.
whys: Noisy people make a lot of sound. That is not about helping.
'Huge' means very big. It does not tell us how she acts.
v.hint: What do we call a person who helps other people?
v.worked: She *always helps her neighbours*, so she is *kind*.

v.q: 'My little brother smiles and says hello to everyone. He is ______.' Choose the best word.
whys: A quiet person does not talk much, but he says hello to everyone.
'Tiny' is about size, not about how he acts with people.
v.hint: Read what he does. Which word matches it?
v.worked: He *smiles and says hello to everyone*, so he is *friendly*.

v.q: 'Nobody talks in the reading room. It is very ______.' Choose the best word.
whys: A room where nobody talks is not noisy.
'Friendly' describes people, not rooms.
v.hint: Think about the sound in the room.
v.worked: *Nobody talks*, so the room is *quiet*.

v.q: 'My kite has red, blue, green and yellow stripes. It is ______.' Choose the best word.
whys: Kites don't make much noise, but the sentence is about colours.
'Helpful' describes a person who helps you.
v.hint: The sentence lists a lot of colours. Which word means that?
v.worked: *Red, blue, green and yellow* is a lot of colours, so it is *colourful*.

v.q: Type the missing linking word (and, but or because).
lines: I like my coach {0} she is very patient.
v.hint: Is the second part a reason?
v.worked: 'She is very patient' is the reason, so we use *because*.

v.q: Type the missing linking word (and, but or because).
lines: Our car is very old, {0} it still goes fast.
v.hint: Old cars are often slow. Is the second idea a surprise?
v.worked: 'Old' and 'still goes fast' are different ideas, so we use *but*.

title.vi: Các ý và to + động từ

v.q: 'Grandpa uses his big basket ______ fruit from the market.' Choose the best words.
whys: We don't say 'uses his big basket carrying fruit'. Use 'to' + verb to say what it is for.
'Carried' is the past, but the sentence says what the basket is for.
v.hint: What is the basket for? Use: to + verb.
v.worked: 'His big basket *to carry* fruit' tells us what the basket is for.

v.q: 'This telescope has a long tube ______ the stars.' Choose the best words.
whys: 'Has a long tube sees' is not a correct sentence.
We don't say 'a long tube seeing the stars' to give a use.
v.hint: To say what something is for, use: to + verb.
v.worked: 'A long tube *to see* the stars' tells us what the tube is for.

v.q: The task asks: who the person is, what he or she is like, what he or she does, why the person is special. Which bullet point is missing from Joe's answer?
opts: why she is special to Joe
whys: 'She is kind and funny' tells us what she is like.
'She waters her flowers' tells us what she does.
v.hint: Look for a reason with 'because'.
v.worked: Joe never says why his grandma is special, so the last bullet point is missing.

stim.head: Joe's answer
stim.html: My grandma is sixty-five. She is kind and funny. Every morning she waters her flowers, and then she cooks breakfast for us.

v.q: The task asks: who the person is, what he or she is like, what he or she does, why the person is special. Which bullet point is missing from Sara's answer?
opts: why he is special to Sara
whys: 'My neighbour lives next door' tells us who he is.
'He is special to me because ...' is her reason.
v.hint: Look for describing words like kind, funny or friendly.
v.worked: Sara has no describing words, so 'what he is like' is missing.

stim.head: Sara's answer
stim.html: My neighbour lives next door with his dog. He grows vegetables and gives some to us. He is special to me because he teaches me about plants.

v.q: The task asks: what it is and where, what it looks like, one special feature and its use, why you like it. Which bullet point is missing from Hannah's answer?
opts: a special feature and its use
whys: 'Huge and white, with a round roof' tells us what it looks like.
'I love it because I can learn about planets' is her reason.
v.hint: Look for 'to + verb'. Does Hannah say what something is for?
v.worked: Hannah does not say one special feature or what it is used for.

stim.head: Hannah's answer
stim.html: The space museum is in the centre of my city. It is huge and white, with a round roof. I love it because I can learn about planets there.

v.q: The task asks: what it is and where, what it looks like, one special feature and its use, why you like it. Which bullet point is missing from Bach's answer?
opts: a special feature and its use
whys: 'Our family's kite' and 'in the garage' tell us what it is and where.
'A long string to fly it high' is the special feature and its use.
v.hint: Look for an opinion and 'because'.
v.worked: Bach never says why he likes the kite, so the last bullet point is missing.

stim.head: Bach's answer
stim.html: My favourite thing is our family's kite. We keep it in the garage. It is red and yellow, with a long tail. It has a very long string to fly it high in the sky.

v.q: One verb is wrong: 'My dad cook dinner every evening.' Type the correct word.
v.hint: With he, she or 'my dad', the verb needs an ending.
v.worked: 'My dad' is like 'he', so we write *cooks*.

v.q: One verb is wrong: 'Our coach have a loud whistle.' Type the correct word.
v.hint: With he, she or 'our coach', 'have' changes.
v.worked: 'Our coach' is like 'he' or 'she', so we write *has*.

v.q: Which sentence has capital letters and a full stop in the right places?
opts: My aunt lives in Da Nang.
my aunt lives in Da Nang.
My aunt lives in da nang
whys: A sentence must start with a capital letter: 'My'.
Place names need capitals, and the sentence needs a full stop.
v.hint: Check the first word, the names of places and the end.
v.worked: '*My* aunt lives in *Da Nang.*' has a capital at the start, capitals for the city and a full stop.

v.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
whys: The first word of a sentence needs a capital letter.
Days of the week need a capital, and the sentence needs a full stop.
v.hint: Check the first word, the day and the end of the sentence.
v.worked: '*On Saturday* we visit Grandma*.*' has all the capitals and a full stop.

v.q: The task says: Write 6 to 8 sentences. Is Thao's answer the right length?
whys: Count the full stops: there are only 4 sentences.
It has only 4 sentences, so it can't be too long.
v.hint: Count the sentences, then compare with 6 to 8.
v.worked: Thao wrote 4 sentences, so she needs 2 to 4 more, for example a reason with 'because'.

stim.head: Thao's answer
stim.html: My dad is a taxi driver. He is tall and strong. He drives all day. I love my dad.

v.q: The task says: Write 6 to 8 sentences. Is Ivan's answer the right length?
whys: Count again: there are 7 sentences.
It has 7 sentences, and that is not more than 8.
v.hint: Count the full stops, then compare with 6 to 8.
v.worked: Ivan wrote 7 sentences, so it is inside 6 to 8.

stim.head: Ivan's answer
stim.html: My favourite person is my big brother. He is fifteen. He is clever and very funny. He plays the guitar in a band. He also helps me with my maths homework. On Sundays we ride our bikes together. He is special to me because he always has time for me.

blurb.en: Plan, write and compare your answer with three model answers.
blurb.vi: Lên ý, viết bài và so sánh với ba bài mẫu.

tasks.title: My grandma or grandpa
tasks.prompt: Write about your grandma or your grandpa. Write 6 to 8 sentences. Use describing words and linking words.
bullets: Who is this person?
What is he or she like?
What does he or she do?
Why is this person special to you?
starters: She is special to me because ...

models.text: My grandma is sixty years old. she is kind and nice. She live with my family. She cook rice and fish for us every day. She is special because she love me
notes: Task achievement and content 1/2: all four bullets are there, but each one is very short, and the reason 'she love me' is not explained. Only 32 words, so it is a little short.
Organisation and layout 1/2: the order is sensible, but 'because' is the only linking word, so the sentences sound like a list.
Grammar range and accuracy 1/2: the meaning is clear, but 'she' needs the verb with -s: 'she lives', 'she cooks', 'she loves'.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: the words are spelt right, but 'kind and nice' is very simple. Try 'gentle', 'cheerful' or 'clever'.
Writing conventions 1/2: 'she' needs a capital S at the start of a sentence, and the last sentence has no full stop.

models.text: My favourite person in my family is my grandpa. He is seventy years old. He is tall and very funny. Every morning he walks to the market and buys fruit for us. In the evening he tells us stories. He is special to me because he makes me laugh every day.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets, with a clear reason at the end.
Organisation and layout 1/2: one paragraph in a good order, and 'Every morning' and 'In the evening' help. More linking words like 'also' or 'but' would join the short sentences.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: the present simple is correct: 'walks', 'buys', 'tells', 'makes'.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: everything is spelt right, but 'tall and very funny' is simple. One or two more describing words would help.
Writing conventions 2/2: every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

models.text: My grandma is the kindest person in my family. She is small and quiet, but she is very clever. Every morning she waters the colourful flowers in her garden. She also cooks delicious soup for us when we visit. On Sundays she teaches me to sew. She is special to me because she is always patient and she listens to my stories.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets are clear, and the reason is developed: she is patient and she listens.
Organisation and layout 2/2: one clear paragraph in a logical order, joined with 'but', 'also', 'when' and 'because'.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: accurate present simple, a superlative ('the kindest') and 'teaches me to sew'.
Vocabulary and spelling 2/2: varied describing words (quiet, clever, colourful, delicious, patient), all spelt right.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

tasks.title: A sports coach
tasks.prompt: Write about a coach who teaches you a sport at a club. Write 6 to 8 sentences. Use describing words and linking words.
bullets: Who is this person?
What is he or she like?
What does he or she do?
Why is this person special to you?
starters: She is important to me because ...

models.text: My football coach is a young man. He is tall and strong. He teach us to kick and pass the ball. We play at the club every saturday. I like him because he is funy.
notes: Task achievement and content 1/2: all four bullets are there, but the reason 'he is funny' is very short and not explained. Only 35 words.
Organisation and layout 1/2: the ideas are in order, but there is only one linking word ('because').
Grammar range and accuracy 1/2: 'He teach' should be 'He teaches'. With he or she, the verb needs -s or -es.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: 'funy' should be 'funny'. The describing words (tall, strong) are simple.
Writing conventions 1/2: 'saturday' needs a capital S, because days of the week always start with a capital letter.

models.text: My badminton coach works at the sports club near my home. She is friendly and very fast. She teaches us how to hit the shuttlecock high. She also shows us fun games. I play with my team every Saturday. She is important to me because she helps me get better.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets, and a reason with 'because'.
Organisation and layout 1/2: a good order with 'also' and 'because', but most sentences are short and start with 'She'.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: accurate present simple ('works', 'teaches', 'shows') and 'how to hit'.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: a good topic word ('shuttlecock'), but the describing words are simple (friendly, fast, fun). Try 'cheerful' or 'patient'.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

models.text: My skateboarding coach is a cheerful young woman at our neighbourhood club. She is brave, patient and always smiling. Every Sunday she shows us how to turn and jump safely. When I fall, she helps me stand up and try again. She is important to me because she makes me feel brave. Now I am not scared any more.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets are clear, and the reason is developed: she makes me feel brave, and now I am not scared.
Organisation and layout 2/2: one clear paragraph in a logical order, linked with 'When' and 'because', and 'Now' shows the change.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: accurate present simple with varied patterns: 'shows us how to turn', 'helps me stand up'.
Vocabulary and spelling 2/2: lively, varied words (cheerful, patient, safely, scared), all spelt right.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

tasks.title: A neighbour I like
tasks.prompt: Write about a neighbour you like. Write 6 to 8 sentences. Use describing words and linking words.
bullets: Who is this person?
What is he or she like?
What does he or she do?
Why is this person special to you?

models.text: My neighbour is an old lady. She have a white cat and a small garden. She is very friendly she always say hello to me. I like her because she is kind.
notes: Task achievement and content 1/2: all four bullets are there, but they are very short and the reason 'she is kind' is not explained. Only 32 words.
Organisation and layout 1/2: the order is clear, but there is only one linking word ('because').
Grammar range and accuracy 1/2: 'She have' should be 'She has', and 'she always say' should be 'she always says'.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: the words are spelt right, but there are few describing words (old, friendly, kind).
Writing conventions 1/2: 'She is very friendly she always say hello' is two sentences. It needs a full stop after 'friendly'.

models.text: My neighbour is an old man who lives next door. He has grey hair and a big smile. Every morning he waters his plants and feeds the birds. He is friendly. He often gives us mangoes from his tree. I like him because he is kind to everyone in our street.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets, with a reason at the end.
Organisation and layout 1/2: a good order, but 'and' is used a lot. Try 'also' or 'when' to join ideas.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: accurate present simple ('waters', 'feeds', 'gives') and 'who lives next door'.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: everything is spelt right, but 'friendly' and 'kind' are the only words about his character.
Writing conventions 2/2: every sentence has a capital letter and a full stop.

models.text: My favourite neighbour is a young baker on our street. He is tall, cheerful and very hard-working. He gets up at four o'clock to bake fresh bread. When I walk to school, he always waves and says good morning. He also gives us warm rolls on Sundays. I like him because he makes our street a friendly place.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets are clear, and the reason is about the whole street.
Organisation and layout 2/2: one clear paragraph in a logical order, joined with 'When', 'also' and 'because'.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: accurate present simple and an infinitive of purpose: 'gets up at four o'clock to bake fresh bread'.
Vocabulary and spelling 2/2: varied describing words (cheerful, hard-working, fresh, warm), all spelt right.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

tasks.title: An interesting building
tasks.prompt: Write about an interesting building in your town or city. Write 6 to 8 sentences. Use describing words and linking words.
bullets: What is it and where is it?
What does it look like?
What is one special feature, and what is it used for?
Why do you like it?

models.text: The big hotel is in the centre of my city. It is very tall and it have blue windows. It has a pool on the roof. I like it because it is beautifull
notes: Task achievement and content 1/2: it says what and where, what it looks like and why, but it does not say what the pool is used for. Only 34 words.
Organisation and layout 1/2: the order is good, but 'and' and 'because' are the only linking words.
Grammar range and accuracy 1/2: 'it have' should be 'it has'. There is no 'to + verb' to say what the pool is for.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: 'beautifull' should be 'beautiful'. The describing words (big, tall) are simple.
Writing conventions 1/2: the last sentence has no full stop.

models.text: The music academy is a big building near my school. It is white, with tall windows and a red door. Inside, there is a huge hall to give concerts. Students go there to learn the piano and the violin. I like it because the music is beautiful. I want to study there one day.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets: the special feature is the huge hall, and its use is 'to give concerts'.
Organisation and layout 1/2: a logical order and 'Inside' helps, but only 'and' and 'because' join the ideas.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: accurate present simple and two infinitives of purpose ('to give', 'to learn').
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: good words (huge, concerts, violin), but 'big' and 'beautiful' are simple. Try 'grand' or 'tall'.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

models.text: The history museum is my favourite building in our city. It stands next to the river, and it looks like a huge stone boat. It has round windows and a shiny glass roof. The best part is the glass lift. Visitors use it to go up to the top and see the whole city. I like the museum because I always learn something new there.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets are clear: the special feature is the glass lift, and visitors use it to go up and see the city.
Organisation and layout 2/2: one clear paragraph in a logical order, linked with 'and' and 'because'. 'The best part is' introduces the special feature.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: accurate present simple, 'looks like' and an infinitive of purpose ('to go up').
Vocabulary and spelling 2/2: varied words (stone, shiny, round, glass lift, whole), all spelt right.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

tasks.title: An amazing space machine
tasks.prompt: Write about a machine that helps people explore space. Write 6 to 8 sentences. Use describing words and linking words.
bullets: What is it and where is it?
What does it look like?
What is one special feature, and what is it used for?
Why do you like it?

models.text: A rocket is a big machine. It go up into space from the ground. It is white and very tall. It have big engines at the bottom. I like it because it is fast
notes: Task achievement and content 1/2: it says what it is and what it looks like, but it does not say what the engines are used for, and the reason is short. Only 33 words.
Organisation and layout 1/2: the order is clear, but 'because' is the only linking word.
Grammar range and accuracy 1/2: 'It go' should be 'It goes', and 'It have' should be 'It has'.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: the words are spelt right, but they are simple (big, tall, fast).
Writing conventions 1/2: the last sentence has no full stop.

models.text: A satellite is a space machine. It goes around the Earth, high above the clouds. It is small and silver, and it has two long wings. The wings are solar panels to make electricity from sunlight. It also send messages to our phones. I like satellites because they help people talk to each other.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets: the special feature is the solar panels, and they are used to make electricity.
Organisation and layout 2/2: one paragraph in a logical order, joined with 'and', 'also' and 'because'.
Grammar range and accuracy 1/2: mostly accurate, with 'to make electricity', but 'It also send' should be 'It also sends'.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: good topic words (satellite, solar panels, electricity), but 'small' and 'long' are simple.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

models.text: My favourite space machine is the rover that explores Mars. It is far away on a red, rocky planet. It looks like a small car with six big wheels. It has a long metal arm with a drill to dig into rocks. Scientists study the rocks to learn about Mars. I like the rover because it is clever, and it never gets tired.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets are clear: the special feature is the arm with a drill, used to dig into rocks.
Organisation and layout 2/2: one clear paragraph in a logical order, joined with 'that', 'and' and 'because'.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: accurate present simple, 'looks like' and two infinitives of purpose ('to dig', 'to learn').
Vocabulary and spelling 2/2: varied topic words (rover, rocky, drill, scientists), all spelt right.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

tasks.title: A useful thing in my kitchen
tasks.prompt: Write about a useful thing in your kitchen at home. Write 6 to 8 sentences. Use describing words and linking words.
bullets: What is it and where is it?
What does it look like?
What is one special feature, and what is it used for?
Why do you like it?
starters: The most useful thing in our kitchen is ...

models.text: The fridge is in our kitchen. It is big and grey. It has a freezer to keep ice cream cold. i like it because it keep my food fresh and good
notes: Task achievement and content 1/2: all four bullets are there, but each one is very short. Only 31 words, so it needs more detail.
Organisation and layout 1/2: the order is clear, but 'and' and 'because' are the only linking words.
Grammar range and accuracy 1/2: 'to keep ice cream cold' is good, but 'it keep' should be 'it keeps'.
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: the words are spelt right, but they are simple (big, good).
Writing conventions 1/2: 'i' must always be a capital 'I', and the last sentence has no full stop.

models.text: Our rice cooker is in the kitchen, next to the fridge. It is white and round, with a black lid. It has a small button to keep the rice warm. Mum uses it to cook rice every evening. It is very easy to use. I like it because the rice is always soft and hot.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets: the special feature is the button, used to keep the rice warm.
Organisation and layout 1/2: a logical order, but the sentences are short, and only 'because' links two ideas.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: accurate present simple and two infinitives of purpose ('to keep', 'to cook').
Vocabulary and spelling 1/2: everything is spelt right, but the describing words are simple (white, round, soft, hot).
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

models.text: The most useful thing in our kitchen is our blender. It sits on the shelf next to the sink. It is tall and made of clear glass, so you can see inside. At the bottom, it has sharp blades to crush fruit and ice. Every Sunday, Dad uses it to make cold mango smoothies. I like it because the smoothies are delicious and healthy.
notes: Task achievement and content 2/2: all four bullets are clear: the special feature is the sharp blades, used to crush fruit and ice.
Organisation and layout 2/2: one clear paragraph in a logical order, linked with 'so', 'At the bottom' and 'because'.
Grammar range and accuracy 2/2: accurate present simple, a superlative ('the most useful') and two infinitives of purpose.
Vocabulary and spelling 2/2: varied describing words (clear, sharp, cold, delicious, healthy), all spelt right.
Writing conventions 2/2: complete sentences with capital letters and full stops.

items.en: Answer *all four* bullet points. Tick each one when you write about it.
items.vi: Viết đủ *cả bốn* ý. Đánh dấu từng ý khi đã viết xong.
example: Who: *My favourite person is* my aunt.
Why: *She is special to me because* she is kind.

items.en: Use *describing words* to say what a person, place or thing is like.
items.vi: Dùng *từ miêu tả* để nói một người, một nơi hay một đồ vật như thế nào.
example: The museum has a *huge* glass door.

items.en: Join your ideas with *linking words*: and, but, because, so, also, when.
items.vi: Nối các ý bằng *từ nối*: and, but, because, so, also, when.
example: The lamp is small, *but* it is very bright.
He is clever. He is *also* very funny.

items.en: Say what something is for with *to + verb*.
items.vi: Nói một vật dùng để làm gì bằng *to + động từ*.
example: It has a long arm *to pick up* rocks.

items.vi: Kết bài bằng *ý kiến* của em và một *lý do*.
example: I like it *because* it is useful.
She is special to me *because* she always helps me.

items.en: Write *6 to 8 sentences* in one paragraph. Check capital letters, full stops and verbs.
items.vi: Viết *6 đến 8 câu* trong một đoạn văn. Kiểm tra chữ in hoa, dấu chấm và động từ.
example: He *has* a big dog. (not: he have)

check.sentence: In Task 1 and Task 2, I write about {all four|two|three} bullet points.
My neighbour is very {friendly|huge|colourful}. She always says hello.
The lamp is small, {but|because|so} it is very bright.
We use the box {to keep|keeping|keeps} our toys.
I like the museum {because|but|then} I learn a lot there.
My uncle {has|have|having} a big red car.

v.q: 'My uncle makes everyone laugh. He is very ______.' Choose the best word.
whys: A quiet person does not say much. He makes everyone laugh.
'Tired' means he needs a rest. It is not about making people laugh.
v.hint: What kind of person makes people laugh?
v.worked: He *makes everyone laugh*, so he is *funny*.

v.q: 'The hotel has three hundred rooms. It is ______.' Choose the best word.
whys: Three hundred rooms is a lot, so it can't be tiny.
'Funny' is for people or jokes, not buildings.
v.hint: Think about the size of the hotel.
v.worked: *Three hundred rooms* is very, very big, so the hotel is *huge*.

v.q: 'My grandpa is old, ______ he can still run fast.' Choose the best word.
whys: Being old is not the reason he runs fast.
'So' shows a result, but old people don't run fast because they are old.
v.hint: Are 'old' and 'can still run fast' the same kind of idea or different?
v.worked: 'Old' and 'can still run fast' are different ideas, so we use *but*.

v.q: 'I love our garden lamp ______ it is very bright.' Choose the best word.
whys: 'But' joins two different ideas. Being bright is a reason to love it.
'Then' tells us what happens next.
v.hint: Is the second part a reason?
v.worked: 'It is very bright' is the reason, so we use *because*.

v.q: 'The rover has a camera ______ photos.' Choose the best words.
whys: 'Has a camera takes' is not a correct sentence.
We don't say 'a camera taking photos' to give its use here.
v.hint: What is the camera for? Use: to + verb.
v.worked: 'A camera *to take* photos' tells us what the camera is for.

v.q: 'We use the big box ______ our toys.' Choose the best words.
whys: We don't say 'use the big box keeping our toys'. Use 'to' + verb to say what it is for.
'Kept' is the past, but the sentence says what the box is for.
v.hint: To say what something is for, use: to + verb.
v.worked: 'We use the big box *to keep* our toys' tells us what the box is for.

v.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
opts: My uncle has a dog called Spot.
my uncle has a dog called Spot.
My uncle has a dog called spot
whys: The first word of a sentence needs a capital letter.
A pet's name needs a capital letter, and the sentence needs a full stop.
v.hint: Check the first word, the name and the end of the sentence.
v.worked: '*My* uncle has a dog called *Spot.*' has both capitals and a full stop.

v.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
opts: In July we go to Ha Long Bay.
in July we go to Ha Long Bay.
In july we go to ha long bay
whys: The first word of a sentence needs a capital letter.
Months and place names need capitals, and the sentence needs a full stop.
v.hint: Check the first word, the month, the place and the end.
v.worked: '*In July* we go to *Ha Long Bay.*' has all the capitals and a full stop.

v.q: Which word is spelt correctly in British English?
whys: This is American spelling. British English adds a 'u'.
This word needs an 'e' at the end.
v.hint: British English writes 'our' in this word.
v.worked: In British English we write *favourite*.

v.q: Which word is spelt correctly in British English?
whys: This is American spelling. British English adds a 'u'.
'-ful' at the end of a word has only one 'l'.
v.hint: Think of 'colour' and the ending '-ful'.
v.worked: 'colour' + 'ful' = *colourful*.

v.q: The task asks: who the person is, what he or she is like, what he or she does, why the person is special. Which bullet point is missing from Rory's answer?
opts: why she is special to Rory
whys: 'She is special to me because ...' is his reason.
'Clever and very kind' tells us what she is like.
v.hint: Look for things she does, like 'she plays' or 'she helps'.
v.worked: Rory says who she is, what she is like and why, but not what she does every day.

stim.head: Rory's answer
stim.html: My big sister is twelve years old. She is clever and very kind. She has long black hair and brown eyes. She is special to me because she always listens to me.

v.q: The task asks: who the person is, what he or she is like, what he or she does, why the person is special. Which bullet point is missing from Esme's answer?
opts: why he is special to Esme
whys: 'He cooks noodles' and 'he takes me fishing' tell us what he does.
'He is special to me because ...' is her reason.
v.hint: Look for describing words like funny, kind or tall.
v.worked: Esme has no describing words about her uncle, so 'what he is like' is missing.

stim.head: Esme's answer
stim.html: My uncle is a cook in a restaurant. He cooks noodles every day. On Sundays he takes me fishing. He is special to me because he teaches me new things.

v.q: The task asks: what it is and where, what it looks like, one special feature and its use, why you like it. Which bullet point is missing from Layla's answer?
opts: a special feature and its use
whys: 'A big slide to go down into the pool' is the special feature and its use.
'I like it because ...' is her reason.
v.hint: Look for describing words about colours, shapes and size.
v.worked: Layla never says what the hotel looks like, for example its colour or size.

stim.head: Layla's answer
stim.html: There is a tall hotel next to the beach in my town. It has a big slide to go down into the pool. I like it because my family has a holiday there every summer.

v.q: The task asks: what it is and where, what it looks like, one special feature and its use, why you like it. Which bullet point is missing from Hieu's answer?
whys: 'Black and silver, with a tiny blue light' tells us what it looks like.
'I like it because ...' is his reason.
v.hint: Does Hieu say WHERE the lamp is?
v.worked: Hieu never says where the lamp is, for example 'in our garden'.

stim.head: Hieu's answer
stim.html: The lamp is black and silver, with a tiny blue light. It has a solar panel to catch sunlight. I like it because it turns on by itself at night.

v.q: Which is the best last sentence for a text about your grandma?
opts: She is special to me because she always listens.
She has got short grey hair and brown eyes.
She lives in a small house near the river.
whys: This describes what she looks like, but it gives no opinion or reason.
This says where she lives, but it gives no opinion or reason.
v.hint: A good last sentence gives your opinion and a reason.
v.worked: 'She is special to me *because* she always listens' gives an opinion and a reason.

v.q: Which is the best last sentence for a text about a museum?
opts: I like it because I learn something new.
It is next to a big hotel in the city centre.
It has a huge glass door and a red roof.
whys: This says where it is, but it gives no opinion or reason.
This describes what it looks like, but it gives no opinion.
v.hint: Which sentence says what you think and why?
v.worked: 'I like it *because* I learn something new' gives an opinion and a reason.

v.q: 'The lamp is small. It is very bright.' Which sentence joins the ideas best?
opts: The lamp is small, but it is very bright.
The lamp is small because it is very bright.
The lamp is small, so it is very bright.
whys: Being bright is not the reason it is small.
Being small does not make a lamp bright.
v.hint: Are the two ideas different or is one a reason?
v.worked: Small and bright are different ideas, so *but* joins them best.

v.q: 'I love my coach. She is very patient.' Which sentence joins the ideas best?
opts: I love my coach because she is very patient.
I love my coach, but she is very patient.
I love my coach, then she is very patient.
whys: 'But' is for different ideas. Being patient is a reason to love her.
'Then' is for what happens next, not a reason.
v.hint: Is 'She is very patient' a reason?
v.worked: Being patient is the reason, so *because* joins the ideas best.

v.q: The task asks for one special feature and its use. Which sentence is best for a rover?
opts: It has a long arm to pick up rocks.
It is on Mars, far away from Earth.
I like it because it is very clever.
whys: This says where it is, not a special feature and its use.
This is an opinion, not a special feature and its use.
v.hint: Look for 'It has ... to + verb'.
v.worked: 'It has a long arm *to pick up* rocks' gives a feature and what it is for.

v.q: The task asks for one special feature and its use. Which sentence is best for a rice cooker?
opts: It has a button to keep rice warm.
It is white and round, with a black lid.
It is in the kitchen, next to the fridge.
whys: This says what it looks like, not what a feature is for.
This says where it is, not a special feature and its use.
v.hint: Look for 'It has ... to + verb'.
v.worked: 'It has a button *to keep* rice warm' gives a feature and what it is for.
